## Web research: fs.watch cross-platform consistency

Question: "What do the Node.js docs say about fs.watch working the same on every platform?"
Pages: 1 read, 0 not fetched

### Facts
1. The docs say outright that fs.watch does not behave the same on every platform and sometimes cannot be used at all. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "The `fs.watch` API is not 100% consistent across platforms, and is unavailable in some situations."
2. fs.watch only works if the operating system can send file-change notifications. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "This feature depends on the underlying operating system providing a way to be notified of file system changes."
3. Linux uses inotify. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "On Linux systems, this uses inotify(7)."
4. macOS uses kqueue for files and FSEvents for directories. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "On macOS, this uses kqueue(2) for files and FSEvents for directories."
5. Windows uses ReadDirectoryChangesW. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "On Windows systems, this feature depends on ReadDirectoryChangesW."
6. On AIX it needs AHAFS to be enabled, and IBM i does not support it. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "On AIX systems, this feature depends on AHAFS, which must be enabled."
7. IBM i is not supported. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "On IBM i systems, this feature is not supported."
8. Watching can be unreliable or impossible on network file systems and in virtualized host file systems. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "watching files or directories can be unreliable, and in some cases impossible, on network file systems (NFS, SMB, etc) or host file systems..."
9. When notifications are not available, fs.watch may throw an exception. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "then `fs.watch()` will not be able to function and may throw an exception."
10. fs.watchFile is a fallback that polls with stat, but it is slower and less reliable. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "It is still possible to use `fs.watchFile()`, which uses stat polling, but this method is slower and less reliable."
11. On Windows, moving or renaming the watched directory produces no events. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "On Windows, no events will be emitted if the watched directory is moved or renamed."
12. On Linux and macOS, if a watched path is deleted and recreated, events for the new file are not emitted. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "Events for the new inode will not be emitted."
13. Only Linux, macOS, Windows and AIX supply the `filename` argument to the callback. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "Providing `filename` argument in the callback is only supported on Linux, macOS, Windows, and AIX."
14. Even on those platforms, `filename` is not always provided. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "Even on supported platforms, `filename` is not always guaranteed to be provided."
15. The `recursive` option only works on supported platforms. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "This applies when a directory is specified, and only on supported platforms (See caveats)."
16. Recursive watching on Linux, AIX and IBMi was added in v19.1.0. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "Added recursive support for Linux, AIX and IBMi."
17. fs.watch gives no protection against malicious changes to the file system. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "The `fs.watch` API does not provide any protection with respect to malicious actions on the file system."
18. "rename" events are only described as happening "on most platforms." Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "On most platforms, `'rename'` is emitted whenever a filename appears or disappears in the directory."

### Inferences
- The spec should not assume fs.watch behaves the same everywhere. Each target OS and file system will need its own tests (from facts 1–9, 11–15, 18).
- The sync logic needs a fallback for when `filename` is null and for when fs.watch throws (from facts 9, 13, 14).
- Watched paths on network shares or inside Docker or Vagrant need a polling fallback or an alternative to fs.watch (from facts 8, 10).
- An event alone should not be trusted when deciding to sync. The file's state should be checked again before acting on it (from facts 12, 17).

### Not fetched
- None.

### Warnings
- None.

- Q1 Which operating systems and file systems (local, network, container mounts) must the file-sync feature support?
- Q2 What is the minimum Node.js version the feature will run on?
- Q3 What should happen when fs.watch is unavailable or throws on a user's system?
